We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\int (x)(\frac{4{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})-\frac{2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}-\frac{4x{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{8x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}-\frac{4x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+\frac{8x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+8)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{4D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{({log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}))}^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+8)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({e}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})+8)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}({ln}^{2}⁡({1}^{2})-4\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{2})+8) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(4-8+8)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}(0-0+8) \\  & =\frac{4e-8}{{ln}^{2}⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$
